survey: A stylized meteor/asteroid on a blue wavy background. Main parts: (1) a lumpy brown rock body, seen three-quarter from the front-left, with one large crater on the left face, a smaller crater in the middle, a dark crater on the lower edge, small pits and a hairline crack on top; (2) three orange teardrop-shaped flame plumes. They come from the upper-right back edge of the rock and trail up and to the right, each ending in a pointed tip with one or two small droplets. The flames sit on the side away from the direction of travel (down-left), which is how a re-entry trail behaves. The flame bases tuck behind the rock's silhouette and glow slightly onto its edge, so they read as coming from the body, not floating apart from it. The rock floats free with no support, which suits a meteor in flight or in space. The rock is irregular but holds together as one solid mass. Nothing passes through anything else, and there are no loose ends, mirrored parts or countable parts that could be wrong.
